quote: I’m 34 weeks pregnant today, and it’s really settling in that one of the biggest hurdles I’m facing right now isn’t labor, it’s actually navigating family dynamics.
cx: First baby; in-laws watch every Instagram story within minutes.

quote:
As my due date gets closer, all I want is a peaceful, private newborn bubble where my husband and I can figure out parenthood together without feeling like every update, milestone, or moment needs to be shared or observed.  
I also have my first baby shower this weekend, and if I’m being honest, I’m not even excited.
cx: Same post, the week of her shower.

quote: my main practical question: can anyone recommend any books to scare my husband? the birth partner has been so helpful for us. he is super well-informed about labor/birth and feels like he has a job. I would love an equivalent book with some real talk about the birthing person's hormones after delivery, breastfeeding, infant behavior, etc.
cx: 27 weeks, first baby; her husband is reading The Birth Partner as assigned.

quote: i think he's imagining being a super dad whose overwhelming love for the baby makes lack of sleep/existential dread a non-issue. I'm honestly a little jealous that he has access to this fantasy! I feel like all I have ever heard from movies/tv/reddit is that you'll never feel more alone, miserable, and overwhelmed.
cx: Why she wants her husband's expectations of the newborn weeks lowered.

quote: I am worried he’ll feel let down if everything isn’t perfect immediately and I am just looking for a resource that is similar to the birth partner that provides realistic information about what to expect.
cx: Clarifying her ask after a harsh reply.

quote: I can tell it’s getting to him because she coos and smiles with me but not for him and he was SO EXCITED my whole pregnancy and now he just seems so miserable. […] He loves her and tells her all the time but he told me he doesn’t like her right now and that makes me sad :(
cx: A mother posts in a dads' forum; their six-week-old settles only with her.

quote: It doesn’t help that people around me tell me to just let him figure it out and that im “too busy to help another adult with feelings”
cx: What people around her say about supporting her husband.

quote: I think that’s part of what sucks is he thought it’d be this immediate connection and it wasn’t
cx: Same mother on her husband's expectations.

quote: Yes he does skin to skin probably once a day but he’s really warm blooded and that makes her fussier especially during this heatwave
cx: Replying to a suggestion for the father to settle the baby.

quote: Every other week she calls me telling me that she’s got a venue for 200 people, trying to get me to take maternity photoshoot (which my husband and I do not want to do), and is overbearing me with things she wants to happen for the baby shower whether I like it or not.
cx: 29 weeks, first pregnancy; her mother hosts a shower in her hometown.

quote: She started to get upset at me and called me “lazy” for not wanting to stay at the baby shower until midnight. For some reason that’s really hit me, especially being 7 months pregnant.
cx: The shower was to run from 4pm to midnight.

quote:
A few months ago, before I got pregnant, I casually mentioned to my mom that we were trying.  
Her response?  
*“I don’t think you should have another baby.”*
cx: Newly pregnant with her second; afraid to tell her parents after how they treated her first pregnancy.

quote:
People would text me asking about **my baby**, wanting pictures or updates, but almost no one asked **how I was doing**.  
I felt like I wasn’t a person anymore.  
I felt like a walking incubator.
cx: Looking back on the weeks after her first birth.

quote:
**Would it be wrong if I waited to tell my parents until I’m ready?**  
Has anyone else delayed announcing a pregnancy because they were trying to protect their own peace?
cx: Same post.

quote:
I made a comprehensive list of all the things, based on my years of experience, that I will be purchasing.

Bottles

Diapers

A crib

Infant car seat

Baby carrier

The rest of stuff was nonsense and ultimately unnecessary. So if you're a dad to be who is strapped for cash, this is all you need.
cx: A father of two, a third on the way, who gave away all the baby gear.

quote: Yeah but to the exclusion of; monitors, diaper trash disposal, bottle washers, bottle warmers, swings, play mats, and all the other stuff the world made us think we'd need.
cx: What he will not buy a second time.

quote: He doesn’t try and educate himself about baby development (note, we’re very relaxed in general about raising a baby and I’ve only read a couple of books about it. I just try and gain minimal / basic knowledge about milestones and what to expect at what age etc - he has no idea about anything, didn’t even know what “tummy time” was until recently).
cx: UK first-time mother at 9.5 weeks, doing the nights alone.

quote: He is more tired than me although he sleeps through the night as I take care of the baby who wakes up every 1-4 hours. I’ve been living with 4-5 hours broken up sleeps since he was born
cx: Same post: how nights are split.

quote: 3 months ago I started a new job in my home state. My previous job was in a neighboring state. According to multiple resources and customer service reps, I'm unable to file for paid family medical leave for either state. Haven't accumulated enough PTO to give myself some time, either. Anytime I take will be unpaid which we simply cannot afford.
cx: A father laid off and rehired across a state line weeks before the birth.

quote: MA. Need to make a minimal amount in MA the last 4 quarters. Because I worked in NH the previous year, im unqualified for MA paid leave and because im no longer currently working in nh, I dint get paid leave with them, either. It's a joke.
cx: Why neither state's paid leave covers him.

quote: We now have to ask my wife's mother to stay with us  because my wife is having a C-section and she'll need help recovering and caring for our children. Ill have to miss this important time to go to work because we cant afford unpaid leave.
cx: Who will cover the weeks after the birth instead of him.

quote: I didnt even request 3 months either! I asked for 3 weeks and then a partial leave where id take days off here and there only if my wife needed me home
cx: What he asked his employer for.

quote: She’s expressed feeling lonely, sad, and that she’s in a lot of pain. She has also said that she finds it unfair that I get to go have a break while she is left at home alone in the third trimester. However, she told me it’s my decision on what I do.
cx: A husband at 30 weeks planning a friends' trip before their first baby.

quote: It might be a more expensive trip and we are tight on money, but again, this is my last chance to go on a trip before the baby gets here.
cx: His case for a shorter trip.
